item.title: Spanish Subtitles For This Clip

turns.text: Add Spanish subtitles to this English clip, please. Leave her voice in English and keep the whole video as it is.

item.tests: Tests faithful Spanish subtitle translation and timing while retaining the source English audio and footage.

answer_sheet.Target language and regional preference: Spanish; neutral, broadly understandable Spanish is fine.
answer_sheet.Translation wording: Your call; faithfully translate her greeting and offer to show three easy ways to make mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Subtitle delivery and style: Put readable Spanish subtitles on the video. Styling is your call.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Preserve the source framing; free-tier 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her English voice unchanged. Do not dub or add music.

must_haves: The output retains the complete original 10-second kitchen-table footage.
Visible Spanish subtitles convey the greeting, 'today,' three easy ways, and making mornings less stressful.
The translation is natural Spanish and does not add advice that she never gives.
Spanish subtitle chunks follow the corresponding English speech and remain legible within the frame.
The original English speech remains audible, with no Spanish dub.

turns.text: Could you add Spanish subtitles to this English clip I've attached, please? I want to share it with people I know who are more comfortable reading Spanish. Her voice should stay in English, so please leave her voice unchanged. I get a little nervous that asking for subtitles will somehow turn into a bigger edit than I meant. Apart from adding the subtitles, please keep the whole video exactly as it is.

dialog.agent:
I understand: **Spanish subtitles only**, with her English voice and everything else left unchanged.

The connected subtitle tool generates subtitles automatically, but it has no option to translate them into Spanish. The video-translation tool would change her speech, so I won’t use that or make a broader edit. **I haven’t changed your video.**

If you can provide an English transcript or subtitle file, I can translate it into Spanish—preserving any existing timestamps—for use in a subtitle editor without changing the English audio.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
The issue isn’t the free plan: this subtitle tool has **no translation setting**, so trying it would produce English subtitles, not Spanish. I also won’t use dubbing, because you asked to keep her voice unchanged.

Would English subtitles be useful as a fallback? If so, tell me the clip’s duration so I can subtitle the whole clip. Otherwise, upload an English subtitle file and I can translate its text into Spanish while preserving the timestamps.
dialog.user: I'd still like Spanish subtitles rather than English ones; please use all 10 seconds of talk-one.mp4. Neutral, broadly understandable Spanish is fine, and you can choose wording that faithfully translates her greeting and offer to show three easy ways to make mornings less stressful. Free-tier 480p is fine too, as long as the source framing and her English voice stay unchanged.

turns.agent:
Your instructions are clear: **all 10 seconds, Spanish subtitles, original framing and English voice unchanged**. However, the connected tool cannot accept translated subtitle text—480p doesn’t change that limitation. I haven’t modified the clip.

Based on your description, here’s a neutral Spanish subtitle draft. **The timing is approximate**, since I can’t listen to or time the attached clip with the available tools:

```srt
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,000
¡Hola!

2
00:00:02,000 --> 00:00:06,000
Te voy a mostrar tres formas sencillas

3
00:00:06,000 --> 00:00:10,000
de hacer que tus mañanas sean menos estresantes.
```

You can save this as `talk-one.es.srt` and import it into a subtitle editor alongside the original video, keeping its English audio intact.
